sections.h2: Where is Wethersfield, and what kind of town is it?
sections.html:
Wethersfield is a Hartford County town that sits immediately south of Hartford along the Connecticut River, in the Capitol Planning Region. It covers about 13.1 square miles, of which roughly 12.3 are land, and the 2020 census counted 27,298 people.

The town was settled in October 1634 and incorporated on February 21, 1637, alongside Windsor and Hartford. That makes it one of the three oldest English settlements in Connecticut, and it still calls itself "Ye Most Ancient Town in Connecticut." The town uses ZIP code 06109, and Route 99, the Silas Deane Highway, runs through it.

For a seller, the age of the town matters more than the nickname. A town with this much 17th, 18th and 19th century building stock will have owners facing roof, electrical or foundation questions before a conventional buyer's inspector signs off.

sections.h2: What is Old Wethersfield, and how does it affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Old Wethersfield is a National Register historic district, added in 1970, that spans about two square miles and holds roughly 1,100 buildings from the 17th, 18th and 19th centuries. It is described as the largest historic district in Connecticut.

Three buildings in town are individually listed as National Register landmarks: the Buttolph-Williams House on Broad Street, the Joseph Webb House at 211 Main Street, and the Silas Deane House at 203 Main Street. The Webb House is where, in May 1781, George Washington and Rochambeau planned the Siege of Yorktown.

If your house is inside the district, expect buyers to ask about its age, its original windows and any prior alterations. Older framing, knob and tube wiring, oil heat and stone foundations are common questions. Outside the district the stock is mostly 20th century, but the same pattern of deferred maintenance applies. Ask the town's building office what permits are on file for your address before you list, because a missing permit for a finished basement or a replaced furnace can stall a conventional closing.

sections.h2: How is Wethersfield laid out, and which roads matter to buyers?
sections.html:
Interstate 91 is the main highway through town, with exits 25 and 26 serving Wethersfield, and several state routes cross it. Hartford sits directly to the north, which is the main reason many buyers look here.

  • Interstate 91, exits 25 to 26
  • Route 99 (Silas Deane Highway), the main commercial spine
  • Route 175 (Wells Road) and Route 287 (Prospect Street)
  • Route 15 and U.S. Route 5 (Berlin Turnpike and Wilbur Cross Highway)
  • Route 3 (Maple Street and the Putnam Bridge)

Public transit is bus based. CT Transit runs routes 43, 47, 53, 55, 61 and 91 through Wethersfield, and Hartford station is the nearest passenger rail stop. The old rail line through town carries occasional freight trains between Hartford and Old Saybrook.

The town's public schools include Wethersfield High School, Silas Deane Middle School and five elementary schools: Highcrest, Charles Wright, Emerson-Williams, Alfred W. Hanmer and Samuel B. Webb. Corpus Christi School is a private Catholic school for pre-kindergarten through eighth grade, and the CREC Discovery Academy is a STEM magnet.

State government is the largest employer in Wethersfield, followed by the town itself. According to the town's 2021 annual financial report, as summarized on Wikipedia, the top employers were these.

The state's Department of Correction and Department of Motor Vehicles are headquartered here, and the Department of Labor is based on Folly Brook Boulevard. Public employers with hundreds of workers each give the town a steady job base, and several state agencies keep offices in town.

sections.h2: What are the property tax numbers a Wethersfield seller should know?
sections.html:
The town's assessor lists a mill rate of 39.98 for real estate and personal property on the 2025 Grand List, and 32.46 for motor vehicles. The assessment year runs from October 1 to September 30.

Wethersfield finished a state-mandated revaluation for the October 1, 2024 Grand List, and the Town Council adopted a four-year phase-in of the new values. The assessor's own example shows how it works: a property moving from $200,000 to $300,000 in assessment steps up by $25,000 a year, reaching $225,000, $250,000, $275,000 and then $300,000.

The practical effect for sellers is that a buyer's tax bill will keep rising for the remaining phase-in years even if the mill rate holds steady. Anyone comparing offers should ask the assessor's office for the current phased assessment on the specific parcel.

sections.h2: How does the conveyance tax work when a Wethersfield house closes?
sections.html:
Connecticut charges a real estate conveyance tax when a deed is recorded, and the seller's side files the return. The Department of Revenue Services says the grantor, the grantor's attorney or an authorized agent must file Form OP-236 when the price is $2,000 or more, unless an exemption applies.

The return is filed and the tax paid when the deed is recorded. Wethersfield's town code on the state form is 159. The state also lists an exemption for a principal residence sold for less than the mortgages plus the real estate taxes and municipal liens that rank ahead of them, which matters if you owe more than the house will bring.

Rates and municipal shares change, so confirm them with the town clerk or your closing attorney instead of relying on an old figure.

sections.h2: What do Wethersfield sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
The common situations are older houses with deferred repairs, inherited homes held by several heirs, and owners who are behind on taxes or a mortgage. In a town with this much historic building stock, repair lists can run long.

  • Roof, chimney or window work on a house built before 1900
  • A basement or foundation that has seen water, which matters near the river and the Cove
  • Heirs who live out of state and cannot agree on a list price
  • Tax or lien balances that must be paid from sale proceeds
  • Tenants in a multi-family house who are not cooperative on showings

A cash buyer purchases the house in its current condition, so repairs and showings are off the table. The tradeoff is that the offer reflects the work required. Ask for the offer in writing and compare it with what a listing would net after repairs, concessions and months of carrying costs.

sections.h2: What does the town's history tell you about flood and ground risk?
sections.html:
Wethersfield grew on Connecticut River floodplain, and its history includes the 1936 flood pictured in town records summarized on Wikipedia. The town is also home to Great Meadows along the river and the Wethersfield Cove.

Not every house is affected, but a buyer's lender will normally check flood zone status for riverside and low-lying addresses. Check your parcel's flood zone with the town and FEMA before you decide how to sell.

The area's farming past is also worth knowing. Wethersfield was a center of the New England onion trade, and the seed company founded there in 1820 became America's oldest continuously operating seed company, according to Wikipedia.

faqs.q: How many people live in Wethersfield?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 27,298 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate used on this page is 27,291. The town covers about 13.1 square miles south of Hartford.

faqs.q: What is the Wethersfield mill rate?
faqs.a: The town's assessor lists 39.98 for real estate and personal property on the 2025 Grand List and 32.46 for motor vehicles. Confirm the current figure with the Assessor's Office at 860-721-2810 before you rely on it.

faqs.q: Does the 2024 revaluation phase-in affect a buyer's tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The Town Council adopted a four-year phase-in, so a property whose assessment rose is stepped up in equal parts each year. A buyer should ask for the phased assessment that applies to the parcel.

faqs.q: Who files the Connecticut conveyance tax return on a sale?
faqs.a: The seller, the seller's attorney or an authorized agent files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded and the price is $2,000 or more. Wethersfield's town code on the form is 159.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Old Wethersfield as is?
faqs.a: Yes. Nothing in the state conveyance rules requires repairs before a sale, though a conventional buyer's lender and inspector may ask for them. A cash buyer can purchase the house in its current condition.

faqs.q: What if I owe more than the house is worth?
faqs.a: Connecticut's conveyance tax has an exemption for a principal residence when the price does not cover the mortgages and priority tax liens. Talk to your closing attorney about how that applies to your sale.
